newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal PM heads for Mexico to boost trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Portugal PM heads for Mexico to boost trade ties.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres heads for Mexico on Tuesday for a four-day visit in which will he seek to boost trade and tourism between the two countries.
"Officials will focus on ways to promote trade and tourism between Portugal and Mexico, which is very little now," the prime minister's spokesman Miguel Laranjeira told Reuters.
He said Guterres and President Ernesto Zedillo would sign an agreement aimed at promoting tourism in each other's countries.

Economy Minister Augusto Mateus, whose responsibilities include attracting foreign investment to Portugal, will join the Portuguese delegation and hold high-level meetings with Mexican officials and businessmen, Laranjeira said.
The spokesman said the two countries would sign an agreement to abolish visas in diplomatic and official passports.
Guterres will leave Mexico on the same plane as President Zedillo for the Ibero-American summit in Chile from November 9-11, Laranjeira said.
Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio will fly direct from Portugal to Chile for the summit, which will bring together leaders from 21 countries.
